name: Ariwa Sounds
ownershipStory: Neil Fraser, known as Mad Professor, built his own mixing board and opened a four-track studio in his south London living room in 1979, naming it Ariwa after a Nigerian word for sound. He has run it, and released his own and others' dub through it, ever since, making it one of the longest-running independently owned reggae studios and labels in Britain.
hook: A London teenager who fixed radios for a living built his own mixing desk and started the UK's longest-running independent dub label.

blurb.age7: A man built his own recording studio at home in London and used it to make dub music for decades.
blurb.age13: Mad Professor built his own mixing board and opened a tiny studio, Ariwa, in his south London living room in 1979. It is still going, and it made him one of dub's most important producers outside Jamaica.
blurb.adult: Ariwa is the London counterpart to Tubby's Kingston workshop and Perry's Black Ark: another self-built studio-as-instrument, this one continuing the tradition into Britain's reggae diaspora and, later, into collaborations well outside reggae.
